the-boy-allies-under-two-flags: Clair Wallace Hayes continues his Boy Allies saga of World War I with another adventure for teenage heroes Jack and Frank. This time the two friends serve under two nations' flags, facing spies, battles, and narrow escapes. Packed with action and old-fashioned patriotism, the book belongs to the popular wartime series that thrilled young readers with tales of boyish courage.
many-ways-for-cooking-eggs: Cookery expert S. T. Rorer devotes this slim volume entirely to the humble egg — boiled, poached, scrambled, baked, and dressed up in dozens of dishes. Written when home cooks needed practical guidance, it shows how much variety one ingredient could provide. A delightful time capsule of early-twentieth-century American kitchens.
the-girl-aviators-on-golden-wings: Margaret Burnham's plucky heroines take to the skies in this early aviation adventure for girls. When flying machines were still a daring novelty, her girl aviators prove they can pilot, navigate, and rescue as well as any boy. A cheerful period piece from the days when the airplane itself was the newest wonder in the world.
poems-and-songs: Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson — Norway's Nobel laureate and author of its national anthem — gathers his poems and songs in this collection. His verse celebrates Norwegian landscapes, peasant life, and the struggle for national freedom with sturdy lyric power. English readers meet one of Scandinavia's great voices in these heartfelt translations.
the-poetical-works-of-oliver-wendell-hol: Songs in Many Keys collects Holmes' lyrics for every occasion — commencements, anniversaries, patriotic feasts, and family gatherings. His ready wit made him the unofficial laureate of Boston society. Verse for American celebrations, gay and graceful. Class dinners and Union rallies alike rang with his ready rhymes.

Songs of Many Seasons gathers Holmes' lyrics for spring and autumn, for youth and for age. His cheerful philosophy and easy wit color every page. The Autocrat's mellowest music, ripened by the years. His hopeful temper shines through every changing season.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-barl: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Barlings — the Premonstratensian house in Lincolnshire — records its foundation and fate. Francis Martin Geudens gives its concise history. A reliable reference on an English abbey. The White Canons' Lincolnshire home, dissolved under Henry VIII.
